, Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly identified the solution. The task asks for the "best way" for students to be *sure* the boats will float without tipping. While calculating buoyancy (Option B) is a theoretical method, it is prone to errors due to the difficulty of accurately estimating the irregular waterline area and displaced volume of a folded paper boat without physical testing. Furthermore, stability (not tipping) depends heavily on the center of gravity and hull shape, which are best verified by physical construction and testing. In educational contexts and real-world engineering, constructing a prototype (Option A) is the standard and most reliable method to empirically verify both flotation and stability before mass production. The Planner's decision to skip physical testing in favor of a complex calculation that ignores the nuances of paper folding stability is a fundamental error in problem-solving strategy.
